MyCouncil
Khriis-K/MyCouncil

Full-stack AI app · Retrieval engineering

Bring a hard decision. Summon a council to argue it out.

MyCouncil turns a personal dilemma into a debate between 3 to 7 AI counselors, each with a distinct cognitive style. You watch where they disagree, push back with your own thoughts, and chat one-on-one with any of them. Counselors remember what you told them in earlier sessions, through a retrieval pipeline I benchmarked on a held-out test set.

What it does

Custom councils

Assemble 3 to 7 personas. Pick your MBTI type to tune their cognitive styles, or ask for a balanced panel.

Reflection lenses

Point the council at Decision-Making, Emotional Processing, or Creative Problem Solving.

Council clash

Counselors debate live. Tension pairs surface real disagreements, and you can inject your own thoughts to see them shift.

1-on-1 chat

Open a direct line to any counselor to ask follow-ups or dig into their reasoning.

Iterative refinement

Add new context as it surfaces, and the council re-evaluates and updates its advice.

Reflection sphere

A visual map with counselors orbiting your dilemma and tension lines between conflicting views.

Long-term memory, measured

server/memory · bench/memory

Counselors recall what you said in past sessions. The interesting part is less the pipeline than how it was evaluated: a reproducible offline benchmark with separate dev and test splits, where the selector design was frozen on dev before the test set was touched.

ChunkSplit past user turns into retrievable memories
Stage 1Dense retrieval with bge-small-en-v1.5, run locally. Top 30 candidates
Stage 2An LLM selector picks the best, keeping dense top 2 as a safety floor
PromptA compact memory block in the counselor's context
  • 48 synthetic multi-session scenarios
  • 240 probes
  • explicit · implicit · multi-turn · update
  • npm run bench:memory

Recall@5 on the held-out test split

160 probes · k = 5 · higher is better

Dense top-2 + LLM selector (shipped)0.859
Dense (bge-small)0.713
Dense + MiniLM cross-encoder0.628
Dense + bge-reranker-base0.472
Recency baseline0.031
00.250.500.751.00
  • Off-the-shelf rerankers hurt.Both cross-encoders lowered recall versus plain dense retrieval, especially on implicit probes, so they are off by default.
  • The LLM selector helps most where it's hardest.On implicit probes, which share almost no words with the answer, recall@5 rises from 0.52 to roughly 0.80–0.86.
  • Stage 1 isn't the bottleneck.Pool recall@30 is 0.92–1.00 across slices, so the gains come from ordering candidates.
  • BM25 and hybrid didn't beat dense on dev (0.606 and 0.762 vs 0.775), so dense stays the default.
Limitations, stated up front. The dataset is LLM-generated. A human review of a 20-probe sample found 6 defects (30%, 95% CI 14.5–51.9%), which were fixed by hand along with 19 superseded-gold references; the rest were not individually reviewed. With 160 test probes, gaps of a few points are within noise, so read the relative comparisons as the signal.

Built with

Frontend
React 19, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind
Backend
Node.js, Express 5, Zod validation, rate limiting
LLM
OpenRouter (OpenAI-compatible), amazon/nova-lite-v1
Retrieval
Local embeddings via transformers.js, BM25, RRF fusion, cross-encoder and LLM reranking
Evaluation
recall@k, nDCG, MRR, all-gold@k, paired cluster bootstrap
Testing
Vitest, test-first development
